The statement conveys a cautiously positive outlook: labor markets are strong and inflation is near the FOMC’s symmetric 2 percent PCE goal, but household spending has moderated and market-based inflation compensation remains low. In a Taylor-rule and New Keynesian framework, with unemployment below its natural rate and inflation near target, gradual normalization is appropriate, which the Committee signals by maintaining an accommodative stance while anticipating further increases. Evidence on a flatter Phillips curve (e.g., work on core non-tradable inflation) and the role of expectation management supports the Committee’s emphasis on gradualism and anchored longer-term expectations (consistent with VAR-based findings on policy communication and Leeper’s active policy paradigm). Overall tone is balanced but modestly positive rather than exuberant.
